example.title: Try it
example.note: We read a story about a woman named Wangari Maathai.

blocks.text: In Choral Speaking (or Choral Reading), the whole class becomes one big voice. Students bring a story’s conflict to life by speaking it together.

items.text: Students read or watch a short story.
As a class, make a two-column list:
items: Column 1: three phrases the main character might say.
Column 2: three phrases that push back against the main character or create tension.

items.text: The whole class says each phrase together, in unison, one after another.

blocks.text: When thirty voices say the same line at once, the words land with real power. Students feel the weight of each side of the conflict. They also experiment with how volume, pace and expression change the meaning, all without anyone being put on the spot alone. It’s the perfect warm-up for Call and Response.
